How to Summarize a Text

A summary is a cognitive process related to the ability to identify explicit and implicit ideas of a text. To create a summary is necessary to be able to categorize such ideas in a hierarchical order: main idea, secondary ideas, etc., and retell or paraphrase them consequently.

Summarizing a text is simple. These are tips that you can use when reading any kind of text:

1. Read the whole text once to understand the overall meaning.

2. You should try to read between lines in case there is hidden information.

3. Look for the meaning of unusual words on a dictionary.

4. Make a list of the most important points or arguments of the text. You can underline the text or use a highlighter.

5. Organize those key elements in chronological order if it is a story, or in order of importance in other cases.

6. Proofread your summary to see if it is clear.

images.text:
Accessing a database and doing network connection are easier than it sounds; you just need to understand how the database works and how to start it up. </br>
If you want to start the database up, you need to use Oracle Net Services. They are an interface between the database and the network communication protocols. These protocols are in charge of defining how data are transmitted and received. When an application developer creates apps, minor changes should be taken from the database, so it can use the Net services.

Oracle Net is a component that must be installed on both computers, user's and server's, so it can establish the network session. It acts as a courier sending messages from one to the other. </br>
You will need to follow 3 steps if you want to start the session up: first, to start an instance, second, to mount the database, and third, to open the database. Let's have a better look at how this works through an example. </br>
A computer starts the instance with the oracle database; this is the host server. The other computer has an application that runs a user process, this way the client is attempting to connect to the host server.

If the proper Oracle Net Services driver is running, the host server detects the connection and starts a process on behalf of the user. Then, the client should be asked to provide a username or password. This information is recorded in the redo log file. If it is successful, a message is sent, but if the transaction were not successful, the host server would display an error message. </br>
Take into account that other background processes are running; some of them are used to prevent contention, so transactions that use the same data are not required. It is like entering a password multiple times.
